name: Glass Harp: the table by the window
used: Glass Harp (the Waterglass Goose): the background, a table where the glasses stand.
standin: A warm wall, a window with a moon, a lamp's glow and a wooden table, painted in code.
prompt: {STYLE} {SCENE}A cosy old-fashioned room in the evening, seen straight on. A plain warm cream wall with faded patterned wallpaper fills the top three quarters. On the right, a small window (about 74% to 92% across, 10% to 47% down) shows a dusky blue evening sky with a pale moon. On the left, the soft yellow glow of a lamp just out of the picture warms the wall. Across the whole width, a long polished wooden table: its far edge at about 74% down, its top surface a band from 74% to 81% down with a long white lace runner along it, and its plain front panel from 81% to the bottom. The table top is completely bare and the wall above it, between 15% and 78% across, is quiet and plain, because the game stands a row of glasses and the bird there. No glasses, cups, people or animals.

name: Glass Harp: a tumbler, whole and cracked
used: Glass Harp: each glass on the table; the game paints the coloured water inside it, at a different level for each note, and swaps to the cracked one after a wrong tap.
standin: A clear glass outline with a rim ellipse and a glint, drawn in code.
prompt: {STYLE} {SHEET} A 2 x 1 grid of two tall, plain, straight-sided drinking tumblers seen from the side at eye level, very slightly wider at the rim than at the base, each about 260 px wide and 500 px tall: left, the empty glass whole; right, the same empty glass with a jagged crack running down from the rim. Drawn as clear glass: only the outline, the rim ellipse, the thick base and a few white highlights and soft grey reflections; the inside of the glass must be fully transparent (no tint, no fill, no water) so the game can paint water inside it. Same size and position in both cells.

name: Glass Harp: the Goose tapping and honking
used: Glass Harp: the Goose taps a glass with its beak as it plays the tune (and as you tap), and honks with pride when a tune is played back right.
standin: The portrait, leaning towards the glass.
prompt: {STYLE} {VARIANT} The Waterglass Goose (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hoai2k/mini/main/icecreamcone/game/assets/subjects/waterglassgoose.png) in two poses side by side on one sheet, each in its own half, both facing left: left, its long neck bent forward and down so the tip of its beak reaches out to the left at about the height of its own glass body's rim, as if tapping a glass that stands just in front of it; right, its neck stretched straight up, beak open to the sky, honking happily. Body and feet in the same place in both. {ALPHA}

name: Glass Harp: the Goose walking and recoiling
used: Glass Harp: the Goose stepping along the table from glass to glass, and jerking back when a glass cracks or it is too slow.
standin: The portrait, bobbing as it slides along, and shaking and leaning back on a crack.
prompt: {STYLE} {VARIANT} The Waterglass Goose (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hoai2k/mini/main/icecreamcone/game/assets/subjects/waterglassgoose.png) in two poses side by side on one sheet, each in its own half, both facing left: left, walking mid-stride, one long leg lifted and reaching forward, neck held level, the water in its glass body tilting a little; right, recoiling in dismay, neck pulled back in an S, beak open, wings flung up, its water sloshing up the side of the glass. Body at the same height in both. {ALPHA}
